Trenchant

TREN-chuhnt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Trenchant is sharply insightful, forceful, and cutting, especially in criticism or wit.

His trenchant comment during the debate -- pointing out the one flaw in his opponent's entire plan -- silenced the room for a full ten seconds.

Worked Example

Buried in a single trenchant footnote, the academic paper quietly demolished the theory that had dominated the field for a decade.

Trenchant isn't just clever -- it has a cutting edge, like a blade slicing straight through weak reasoning.

How Trenchant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

biting

biting: having a harsh, cutting quality

cutting

cutting: sharp and hurtful in a clever, precise way

Antonyms

mild

mild: gentle, not harsh or forceful

bland

bland: dull, lacking sharpness or force

How Strong Is It? — pointed → trenchant → scathing

pointed vs. trenchant

pointed vs. trenchant: A pointed remark is direct and clearly aimed at something, but it's milder than a fully trenchant one.

scathing vs. trenchant

scathing vs. trenchant: A scathing remark is harshly, often cruelly critical, going even further than a merely trenchant one.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of trenchant.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — trench

root — trench: to cut (Old French trenchier)

suffix — -ant

suffix — -ant: characterized by, having the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Trenchant comes from Old French trenchier ('to cut') + -ant ('characterized by') -- literally 'cutting,' which is exactly the feel of trenchant criticism or wit: sharp enough to cut straight to the point.

Use the root in a new word: retrench

Use the root in a new word: retrench: After a disappointing sales quarter, the company decided to retrench, cutting costs across every department.

Root Check

Word Choice

Trenchant and incisive both describe sharp thinking, but trenchant almost always carries a cutting, critical edge, while incisive praises clear precision without necessarily wounding anyone.
